# Weekly review, 2026-W43 (Mon 10/19 to Fri 10/23): analysis

## Scorecard
- Real -$82.08 (-4.10%), paper -$80.08 (-4.00%), SPY buy-and-hold from the 10/19 close -0.90% (from 10/16: -0.43%). **Behind SPY by 3.2 points.**
- Goal since 10/24: $2,200 and beat SPY. Needed from here: +$282 (+14.7%), +31% on the $917.92 budget above the floor. Odds (judgment): 25-35%.
- One round trip (shot 1, SPY 11/20 790C): -21.9% after peaking at +38% on a closing basis (+47% on the 10/21 pre-close bid). Fees $0.08. No rule was bent.

## Decisions, graded
| When | Decision | Process | Outcome | Quadrant | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sun 10/18 | Take shot 1 Monday on conditions (SPY call), against four WAITs | B- | bad | good thesis, weak structure | The base rate was right and verified, but it was about the index; the call itself doubles ~35% (risk said so) and one contract left no way to bank a gain |
| Mon 10/19 | Buy the 790C when the 785C passed its ceiling; fix the tick bug before sending | B+ | bad | good process / bad outcome | Rules followed, bug caught before any order; the alternate strike was picked pre-open without its own red-team (small) |
| Mon 10/19 | Exits with a -50% stop | C | neutral | weak process | A premium stop on a 0.24-delta call sat ~1% below spot: a noise stop, not a thesis stop |
| Tue 10/20 | Hold | A | good | skill/luck mix | Nothing triggered; the rally attempt held |
| **Wed 10/21** | **Hold through META at +47% with a 7.50-only target** | **D** | **bad** | **bad process / bad outcome** | **The costliest decision ($257 vs the peak). "One contract can't be split" should have meant sell the whole contract at +40-50%, or buy two at entry** |
| Wed 10/21 | Raise the stop to 3.00 (risk-timed for FOMC day) | B+ | good | good / good | Sold at 2.93 vs the 2.195 Friday mark: +$73 vs holding |
| Thu 10/22 | Exit at 14:45 when the stop and the Nasdaq rally-low exit fired together | A | good | good / good | Same-day, live-quote exit as designed |

| Mon 10/19 | Not taking the contrarian's IWM call ("same factor as SPY", n=6 statistic) | B | bad (missed +53%) | good process / bad outcome | Reasonable at the time, but the "same factor" assumption was wrong: IWM +2.0% vs SPY -0.4% |
| All week | No oil/energy position through a Gulf escalation | C | bad (missed USO 180C +66%, COP 150C +40%) | weak process | "Escalation" was never defined in a checkable series, and the Brent trigger read the rolled (January) contract; pacing also blocked it while shot 1 was open (by design) |
| All week | No MSFT/NVDA/AVGO/QQQ buys | A | good | good / good | Those ideas fell 16-42% |

## What went well (repeatable?)
- **Safety and verification (yes, built in):** the gate and the risk red-team caught three sizing/cap bugs and a tick bug before money moved; we caught the META headline-vs-filing gap, the NVDA date and the VIX level.
- **Exit discipline (yes):** both exits ran the same day at 14:43 on live quotes; the raised stop beat holding by $73.
- **Triggers that filter (yes, when tight):** the risk-tightened TLT conditions kept us out of a -28% move.
- **Not buying the consensus AI trade (partly luck):** MSFT, NVDA, AVGO and QQQ ideas all fell; we waited for MSFT's dated print instead.

## What went badly (root cause)
1. **Exit design (structure):** a +47% gain given back, $257 vs the peak. One contract, a 2x-only target, a trailing stop added only at +38%. Fixed mid-week in the playbook (2+ contracts, bank part, stop to cost past +40%); not yet tested.
2. **Consensus bias (thesis + process):** the winners were the dissents (contrarian IWM +53% and USO +66%, momentum's COP +40%, macro's TLT 82C +25%); every higher-confidence AI/mega-cap/SPY idea lost 16-42%. Stated confidence ran *inverse* to outcome. Nothing in the process asked whether an idea was simply the crowd's.
3. **Data (data + process):** a Brent trigger on the wrong contract; Thursday's numbers carried into Friday's brief; META's +3.4% after hours read as support (it closed -7.0%); early VIX and NVDA-date errors.
4. **Execution gap (minor):** the paper model stamps 15-minute-delayed quotes; real fills were $13 worse on the buy and $11 better on the sale (net $2).

**The dissent that was right:** the contrarian's rotation calls, and the four WAITs against the Monday SPY shot.
